commit_message: GATE-07: Mode A Internet gateway — policy enforcement, SSRF protection, signed measurements, audit events
scope_completed: DNS policy: checkResolvedIp() for post-DNS-resolution blocking (defeats DNS rebinding)
Destination allowlist: matchAllowlist() with exact + wildcard matching
Private/loopback/link-local/SSRF blocking: isLoopback, isLinkLocal, isPrivateAddress, isSsrfTarget, isBlockedIp (before + after DNS)
Per-peer quota: bounded per 60-second window with reset
Global quota: bounded per 60-second window with reset
Bandwidth shaping: per-second byte tracking with reset
Revocation: revokedPeers list checked before any other policy
Signed service measurements: signServiceMeasurement + verifyServiceMeasurement (Ed25519 over canonical CBOR with domain tag SHARENET/GATEWAY/MEASUREMENT/1)
Structured audit events: GatewayAuditEvent with type/decision/reason/detail/timestamp
No open-proxy behavior: OPEN_PROXY_FORWARD_FORBIDDEN architecture guard + evaluateGatewayRequest as the ONLY entry point
27 unit tests covering all guards + measurements + audit events
protocol_adr_references: spec/09-internet-gateway.md (gateway model: capability ≠ policy ≠ authorization ≠ capacity ≠ measurement)
known_limitations: Real external HTTPS request through A → Relay(s) → Gateway is deferred — the unit tests prove the policy enforcement layer with in-memory state. The integration test will exercise the full circuit → gateway → real HTTPS path once the mini-services support the 3-message handshake + circuit setup + gateway forwarding.

The gateway policy layer is in reference/ (protocol core, no DB dependency). The service-layer DB-backed implementation in src/lib/sharenet/gateway.ts is the existing stub from the first deliverable; it should be updated to use the new reference/gateway/ types in a follow-up.
DNS resolution is not performed by the reference module — it accepts a resolved IP from the caller and checks it. The actual DNS lookup happens in the service layer (or mini-service).
Bandwidth shaping is informational (tracking only) — actual traffic shaping (token bucket, queue management) is not yet implemented.
